queries.hook: The wish to understand what these texts teach, and to find in them something steady to lean on.
queries.diagnose: When life is lived only for what passes, the heart feels empty; meaning is missing when we forget what does not pass.
queries.steady: What passes cannot fill the heart; turning toward what lasts gives each day a quiet purpose.
queries.act: Turn toward what lasts: serve, study, reflect daily, and offer your work to something beyond yourself.
queries.story: A story of a student who came to a teacher with questions and was led, step by step, toward the truth.

hook.speaker: Bhartrihari
hook.setting: From the section praising learning: the blessings of a good life.
hook.sanskrit: सूनुः सच्चरितः सती प्रियतमा स्वामी प्रसादोन्मुखः स्निग्धं मित्रमवञ्चकः परिजनो निष्क्लेशलेशं मनः । आकारो रुचिरः स्थिरश्च विभवो विद्यावदातं मुखं तुष्टे विष्टपकष्टहारिणि हरौ सम्प्राप्यते देहिना ॥
hook.line: A good child, a loving spouse, a kind boss, a true friend, a mind at ease: count these as grace.
hook.translation: A son of good conduct, a devoted and loving wife, a gracious master, an affectionate friend, kinsfolk who do not cheat, a mind without a trace of strain, a pleasing form, lasting prosperity, a face bright with learning: these come to the one with whom Hari, remover of the world's troubles, is pleased.
hook.why: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
prasang.summary: Bhartrihari praises learning as wealth no thief can take and speech as the one lasting ornament, then turns to good company and the three kinds of people who face obstacles. It ends with the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
prasang.lesson: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.

alternates.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
alternates.setting: Letter from Alameda, California, 18 April 1900, after laying down his role as leader.
alternates.line: I am glad I was born, glad I suffered so, glad I did make big blunders, glad to enter peace.
alternates.translation: I am glad I was born, glad I suffered so, glad I did make big blunders, glad to enter peace.
alternates.why: Honest looking back, with gratitude for the mistakes, can bring peace.

prasang.title: 'I am drifting': a letter from Alameda (1900)
prasang.summary: Two years before his death, worn out, he writes that he has laid down the role of leader. He is glad he was born, glad he suffered, glad he made big blunders. He admits that ambition, personality, fear and love of power lay behind his work, and says they are fading as he drifts toward peace.
prasang.lesson: Honest looking back, with gratitude for the mistakes, can bring peace.

alternates.speaker: Bhartrihari
alternates.setting: From 'Worship of Shiva': gratitude for a simple life.
alternates.sanskrit: यदेतत्स्वच्छन्दं विहरणमकार्पण्यमशनं सहार्यैः संवासः श्रुतमुपशमैकव्रतफलम् । मनो मन्दस्पन्दं बहिरपि चिरस्यापि विमृशन् न जाने कस्यैष परिणतिरुदारस्य तपसः ॥
alternates.line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?
alternates.translation: This freedom to wander at will, food eaten without humiliation, living among noble people, learning whose only fruit is calm, a mind that stirs only gently even when it looks outward for long: I do not know what generous austerity this is the fruit of.
alternates.why: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Worship of Shiva
prasang.summary: Devotional verses longing for a quiet life by the Ganga in Shiva's presence, including a famous non-sectarian line that Shiva and Vishnu are one in essence.
prasang.lesson: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

verse.try_today: Count one blessing around you before the day ends.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verse.sanskrit: प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते । प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥
verse.line: When the mind clears, sorrows start to dissolve, and understanding settles quickly.
verse.translation: In that clarity all sorrows come to an end; for one whose mind is clear, understanding soon becomes steady.

words.en: of one with a clear mind

verse.why: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

prasang.title: The person of steady wisdom
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

verse.for_you: You have found a moment of quiet. In this clarity, sorrows dissolve. Let this steady understanding settle in you today.
verse.try_today: Notice how your understanding settles when your mind is at peace.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on devotees who find joy together and the light he gives them.
verse.sanskrit: मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम् । कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च ॥
verse.line: Their minds on me, they talk of me with each other, and find joy and contentment in it.
verse.translation: With minds fixed on me and lives given to me, enlightening one another and always speaking of me, they are content and delighted.
verse.why: Good company and an inner lamp clear the dark.

prasang.title: The yoga of devotion and its fruit
prasang.summary: Devotees talk of the divine with each other and find joy; out of compassion Krishna lights the lamp of knowledge in their hearts.
prasang.lesson: Good company and an inner lamp clear the dark.

verse.meaning: Devotees who fix their minds on the divine and give their lives to him, teaching one another and always speaking of him, find contentment and delight, as if meeting a beloved. The divine compassionately lights the lamp of knowledge in their hearts.
verse.for_you: You wish to fix your mind on the divine and give your life to him. You find joy in speaking of him and in meeting others who share this light.
verse.try_today: Speak one kind word to another today.

why: mind and life given to him

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
verse.sanskrit: कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः । लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
verse.line: Janaka and others reached fulfilment through action. Keep working, if only for the good of the world.
verse.translation: Janaka and others attained perfection through action alone. And looking to the welfare of the world, you too should act.
verse.why: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

prasang.title: Even the wise, even God, act for the world's sake
prasang.summary: The one content in the self has nothing left to gain, yet the wise, like Janaka and Krishna himself, keep working because others follow their example.
prasang.lesson: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

verse.for_you: Your granddaughter arrived healthy, and you want to offer thanks. That gratitude is a quiet action that already holds the world together. Let this feeling of thanks guide your day.
verse.try_today: Notice one small way to act for the good of the world today.

why: acting for the holding together of the world

verse.speaker: Teacher
verse.setting: The most quoted lines of the graduation address.
verse.sanskrit: देवपितृकार्याभ्यां न प्रमदितव्यम् । मातृदेवो भव । पितृदेवो भव । आचार्यदेवो भव । अतिथिदेवो भव ।
verse.line: Treat your mother as divine, your father as divine, your teacher as divine, your guest as divine.
verse.translation: Do not neglect your duties to the gods and the ancestors. Let your mother be a god to you. Let your father be a god to you. Let your teacher be a god to you. Let your guest be a god to you.
verse.why: Truth, right action, gratitude and graceful giving: a whole life in one speech.
verse.misuse: Honouring parents does not mean accepting mistreatment or giving up your own conscience.

prasang.title: The graduation address
prasang.summary: As a student finishes his studies and leaves to start family life, the teacher gives him parting instructions: speak truth, do right, keep learning, honour mother, father, teacher and guest, give with grace. He even tells the student to copy only the teachers' good conduct, and when in doubt to act as thoughtful, gentle people would.
prasang.lesson: Truth, right action, gratitude and graceful giving: a whole life in one speech.

verse.try_today: See one person today as a guest of God.
verse.scene_line: You hold your newborn granddaughter as a guest of God.

why: the guest and the elder are served as sacred

verse.speaker: Sampati
verse.setting: The monkeys despair at the ocean; the old vulture Sampati rouses them.
verse.sanskrit: पापिउ जाकर नाम सुमिरहीं। अति अपार भवसागर तरहीं॥ तासु दूत तुम्ह तजि कदराई राम हृदयँ धरि करहु उपाई ॥
verse.line: Drop your timidity. Keep Ram in your heart and find a way.
verse.translation: Even sinners who remember his name cross the boundless ocean of the world. You are his messengers: give up your timidity, keep Ram in your heart and find a way.
verse.for_you: You are a messenger of grace. Hold this gratitude in your heart and let it guide your steps forward.
verse.try_today: Hold this feeling of thanks in your heart as you move through the day.

why: act with Ram held in the heart

story.title: The Kols and Kirats have nothing fit to offer and offer it
story.story_hook: Their best hospitality was a promise not to steal his pots. He was delighted.
story.summary: Word spreads through the forest that a prince has come to live among them. The hill people come with leaf-cups of berries, roots and honey, as if they had found treasure. They are painfully aware of who they are and who he is.
story.teaser: Their best hospitality was a promise not to steal his pots. He was delighted.
story.for_you: The new life you hold is its own offering. You do not need to polish your thanks. What you are is enough for this moment.
